title: The Master Algorithm
subtitle: How the Quest for the Ultimate Learning Machine Will Remake Our World
pitch: A tour of the five schools of machine learning and a bet that one universal learning algorithm could one day learn anything from data.

chapters.g: Learning algorithms already shape what we buy, watch and read.
The idea of one learner that could discover any knowledge from data, and why it might exist.
The symbolists: learning rules by logic, and the old puzzle of how we can generalise at all.
The connectionists: neural networks and backpropagation, inspired by the brain.
The evolutionaries: genetic algorithms and programs that evolve.

chapters.t: In the church of the Reverend Bayes
chapters.g: The Bayesians: learning as updating beliefs with probability.
The analogizers: learning by similarity, from nearest neighbours to support vector machines.
Finding structure in data without labels, such as clustering.

chapters.t: The pieces of the puzzle fall into place
chapters.g: Domingos sketches how the five schools could be combined into one learner.

chapters.t: This is the world on machine learning
chapters.g: What a world run on learning machines could look like, for better and worse.

ideas: Machine learning has five main tribes: symbolists, connectionists, evolutionaries, Bayesians and analogizers.
Each tribe has a master method and a blind spot.
A unified learner might combine their strengths.
Learning machines will reshape science, business and daily life.

args.a: A single master algorithm is possible and worth seeking.
args.c: Deep learning's later success came from scale and data more than from unifying the tribes, and some doubt one universal learner exists in a useful form.

args.a: The main risk is people misusing learning machines, not machines turning on us.
args.c: Many alignment researchers argue powerful learners could pursue goals we did not intend, which is a risk in itself.

questions: Which of the five tribes does today's AI most resemble?
Is learning from data enough for general intelligence?
Who should control the data that learning machines use?

quiz.w: Connectionists model learning on the brain.

o: A hypothetical learner that can learn anything from data
quiz.w: It is the book's central idea.

quiz.q: What does the Bayesian school do?
quiz.w: Bayes' rule is the core tool.
